newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen opening mixed.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen opening mixed.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to be mixed at the open Thursday, digesting a slew of economic data while remaining cautious ahead of a key employment report due out tomorrow.

Gross domestic product growth rose an above-forecast 2.2 percent in the second quarter, but the price deflator posted its smallest gain since 1964. Weekly jobless claims fell more than anticipated, to 277,000 claims.
"At first blush, this data contains both good and bad news for markets," Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany, said.
"Some might argue that the second quarter GDP figure was stronger than forecast, but the price deflator is a bit lower than expected," he said. "I was also stunned by the drop in jobless claims."
Analysts said the stock market could see some early profit-taking after rallying to record highs on Wednesday.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index moved out of negative territory, gaining 1.45 points to 958.50. The long bond firmed 8/32 to yield 6.31 percent.
The market faces employment data for July on Friday, which will offer insight into the third quarter, analysts said.
